title: docs(spec): the `routes` retire text and three published pages stop sending app authors to an imperative `http.server` route — apps declare `apis:`, compute in flows, register stack functions (ruling C′ on #23128)
body:
Filed by the director seat (summon #37, `session_01LqNgdPZB2Jnr5HpGbaqLeB`) on the maintainer's ruling C′ on #23128 (「同意」, recorded at 6142279866) under 「立卡你决定，不需要我同意」: the seat files, the lane claims, dispatches and lands. ⛔ Not a claim. Filing gate ③ (a consequence of a ruling). Governed: `packages/spec` prose only (`Clause-②: no`: a retire message and three doc pages; no key, no accept set moves), plus `content/docs/**`.

## What is wrong today
`manifest.contributes.routes` was retired in spec 17 (ADR-0049, `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts:884`), and its retire text still tells an app author: "A route that needs real handler CODE is mounted imperatively: resolve the `http.server` service from the plugin context and register the handler on `kernel:ready`." The same sentence is published in `content/docs/references/api/metadata.mdx`, `package-api.mdx` and `kernel/manifest.mdx`. That door was never finished for app code: a code-mounted route gets no caller identity, no ADR-0069 auth gate, no rate limit, no namespace carve-out and no OpenAPI (#23128's dev report 6138940364); the only in-tree app that followed the sentence is the showcase's `recalc-endpoint.ts`, which answers 500 on every call. The ruling: the imperative route is the platform's own door-building primitive, not an app-author surface.

## What to build (one PR)
1. `manifest.zod.ts:884`'s retire message: replace the imperative sentence with the app-author rule: an app declares `defineStack({ apis })` (`object_operation` or `flow`, ADR-0121), computes in a flow, and registers code as a stack function (`defineStack({ functions })` → `registerFunction`) or a connector; it does not mount routes on `http.server`.
2. The three published pages: the same sentence, regenerated or edited wherever the retire text is rendered (`package-api.mdx:237` is a generated row; say which of the three are generated and regenerate them with the repo's tooling).
3. Nothing else: `http.server` (`core-service-contracts.ts`) and the platform plugins that mount on it are untouched; no key is added or removed.

## Acceptance
- `git grep -n "mounted imperatively" -- packages/spec content/docs` finds nothing; the spec's own tests over retired-key messages pass; `check:generated` (if the pages are generated) and the docs gates exit 0; the manifest reference page renders the new sentence.

Related: #23128 (ruling C′) · ADR-0121 · ADR-0096 · ADR-0049 · `examples/app-showcase/src/system/apis/index.ts`.
